The State Emergency Service advises that people should:
* Move vehicles under cover or away from trees;
* Secure or put away loose items around your property.
* Stay indoors, away from windows, while conditions are severe.

warning-info.text: The next Severe Weather Warning will be issued by 11:00 pm ACST Sunday.

text.p: Check https://www.bom.gov.au/weather-and-climate/warnings-and-alerts. Warnings are also available through TV and Radio broadcasts or call 1300 659 210. The Bureau and State Emergency Service would appreciate warnings being broadcast regularly.

forecast-period.text: Damaging winds possible about the northern Eyre Peninsula, Yorke Peninsula and Flinders Ranges this evening.

text.p: Weather Situation: A cold front extending from a low-pressure system in the Bight is moving across the state today, bringing a gusty west to southwesterly change. A secondary trough is crossing western Eyre Peninsula this afternoon, strengthening winds for a period.

DAMAGING WINDS averaging 55 to 65 km/h with peak gusts of around 90 km/h are possible about coastal parts of western Eyre Peninsula. DAMAGING WIND GUSTS of around 90 km/h are also possible for the northern Yorke Peninsula and further inland in the North West Pastoral. Conditions are forecast to ease below warning thresholds by late Sunday evening.

DAMAGING WINDS averaging 60 to 75 km/h with peak gusts of around 110 km/h are likely about the higher parts of the Flinders Ranges from late Sunday afternoon, easing below warning thresholds by around sunrise on Monday morning.
Locations which may be affected include Ceduna, Hawker, Jamestown, Woomera, Kadina, Burra, Arkaroola, Peterborough and Streaky Bay.
Severe weather is no longer occurring in the Lower Eyre Peninsula district and the warning for this district is CANCELLED.
